prompt_text: I want to try a tanning salon in Charlotte. Which specific salons should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: What is the best tanning salon in Charlotte NC?
answer_verbatim:
Do you mean UV tanning beds/booths, spray (sunless) tans, or both? Also — which part of Charlotte (Uptown, SouthPark, Ballantyne, NoDa, University area, etc.) and what’s your budget/comfort level with UV exposure? With that I can give 4–6 specific salons to call nearby. 

While you decide, here’s a quick, practical plan you can use right away to find a good place and what to ask when you call:

What to look for / why it matters
- UV vs spray: Spray tans are safer (no UV). If you want a natural-looking, instant-free option, choose spray. If you specifically want a bed tan, check bed type and time limits.  
- Cleanliness & safety: Look for freshly cleaned beds/booths, disposable or sterilized mouth/nose protection for spray, and staff who explain aftercare.  
- Technician experience: For spray/airbrush, ask how long the tech has been doing tans and whether they can show before/after photos.  
- Solutions and equipment: For spray, ask which brand (organic/vegan/hypoallergenic options). For beds, ask bed brand (stand-up vs lay-down, levels of UV) and maintenance schedule.  
- Pricing & specials: Ask about single sessions, packages, membership models, and first-time specials.  
- Reviews & photos: Recent Google and Yelp reviews and Instagram photos are useful for real examples.

Script — what to ask when you call
1. “Do you offer spray tans, UV tanning beds, or both?”  
2. (If spray) “Is the spray airbrush or automated? What products do you use? Are techs certified and can you send before/after pics?”  
3. (If UV) “What types of beds do you have (stand-up/lay-down, level of bulbs)? How long are sessions, and how do you determine the right starting level for a new client?”  
4. “How do you clean booths between clients?”  
5. “Do you offer a first-time client special or package deals?”  
6. “Are there any contraindications (medications, skin conditions) I should know about?”  

Red flags to avoid
- Vague answers about cleaning or solution ingredients.  
- No clear pricing or pushy membership sales.  
- No portfolio or before/after photos for spray techs.  
- Staff unable or unwilling to explain safety/aftercare.

If you tell me which neighborhood or zip code and whether you prefer UV or spray, I’ll list 4–6 specific salons in Charlotte to call (with short reasons why to try each).
